rRNA.description: Every locus RefSeq types as rRNA in this annotation: six complete 5S genes plus ten 16S or 23S entries that RefSeq itself flags partial. The truncation is the assembly's and not the biology's, this being a draft contig-level assembly in which the repeated rrn operons broke across contig boundaries. E1179_RS20485, E1179_RS22545, E1179_RS22590 and E1179_RS22605 are fragments of a ~1542 bp 16S; E1179_RS02975, E1179_RS07740, E1179_RS22505, E1179_RS22570, E1179_RS22600 and E1179_RS22615 are fragments of a ~2904 bp 23S. An E. coli K-12 derivative carries roughly seven 16S, seven 23S and eight 5S genes, so summing reads over this list counts a genuine but incomplete and partly truncated rRNA complement.
rRNA.source: Membership is RefSeq's own gene_biotype in the registered GTF. The 16S, 23S or 5S identity of each bare locus tag comes from the product qualifier on the matching rRNA feature in GCF_004354945.1_ASM435494v1_genomic.gff.gz, cross-checked against Rfam RF00177 (16S), RF02541 (23S) and RF00001 (5S) and against the sequence lengths in the assembly's rna_from_genomic FASTA. Nothing was moved to rRNA_pseudogene: that GFF carries no pseudo flag and no rRNA_pseudogene biotype on any of the sixteen, and its partial, start_range and end_range flags record truncation at a contig edge rather than doubt about function. No Mt_rRNA category is emitted because a bacterium has no mitochondrion.
